t: Why TypeScript picks the second overload

t: TypeScript 6 vs 7 on type-fest
k: How much faster does TypeScript 7 type-check a real, type-heavy library than TypeScript 6, and how much of the gain comes from the native compiler itself rather than parallel checking? What happens to memory on a heavy workload? On an Apple M3 Pro (12 cores), TypeScript 7.0.2 checked the type-fest sources 3.5× faster than TypeScript 6.0.3 (0.484 s vs 1.67 s): 2.6× comes from the native compiler alone (single-threaded) and 1.3× from parallel checking. On the full suite with type tests, TypeScript 6 stops at Node.js's default heap limit (4.0 GiB); with a 16 GiB heap it finishes in 74.6 s, against 14.1 s for TypeScript 7 (5.3× faster), but TypeScript 7 peaks higher in memory (11.6 GiB RSS vs 10.4 GiB). Stays open until a second machine is measured with the same protocol. lab #002

t: Typed events: the elegant type that slowed down every call site
k: Does a mapped type with an `as` clause, indexed at every call site, make type-checking measurably slower than inferring the event name from a generic parameter? Yes. Inferring the event name from the generic parameter cut check time by about 40% with TypeScript 6 and by about 65% with TypeScript 7, with the same type safety. Narrowing `include` to `src` also stopped TypeScript from reading a generated file the app never imports. lab #001
